option.name: -b
tip: Specify the size of blocks in bytes.
Valid sizes are powers of two from 1024 to 65536.

option.name: -c
tip: Check the device for bad blocks before creating the file system.
Specify twice for a slower read-write test.

option.name: -C
tip: Specify the cluster size in bytes for bigalloc file systems.

option.name: -d
tip: Copy the contents of the directory or tarball into the file system root.

option.name: -D
tip: Use direct I/O when writing to the disk.

option.name: -e
tip: Set the kernel behavior when errors are detected.
Possible values: continue, remount-ro, panic

option.name: -E
tip: Set comma-separated extended file system options.
See mke2fs(8) for the supported options.

option.name: -F
tip: Force mke2fs to create a file system even when the device or parameters look wrong.

option.name: -g
tip: Specify the number of blocks in a block group.

option.name: -G
tip: Specify how many block groups are packed into a larger virtual block group.

option.name: -i
tip: Specify the bytes/inode ratio.

option.name: -I
tip: Specify the size of each inode in bytes.

option.name: -j
tip: Create the file system with an ext3 journal.

option.name: -J
tip: Set comma-separated journal options such as size=, device= or location=.

option.name: -l
tip: Read the bad blocks list from the file.

option.name: -L
tip: Set the volume label, up to 16 bytes.

option.name: -m
tip: Set the percentage of blocks reserved for the super-user.

option.name: -M
tip: Set the last mounted directory for the file system.

option.name: -n
tip: Do not create a file system; only display what would be done.

option.name: -N
tip: Override the number of inodes to reserve.

option.name: -o
tip: Override the creator operating system field.

option.name: -O
tip: Create the file system with the given features.
Prefix a feature with ^ to disable it.

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet execution.

option.name: -R
tip: Deprecated spelling of -E.

option.name: -S
tip: Write only the superblock and group descriptors.

option.name: -t
tip: Specify the file system type to create.
Possible values: ext2, ext3, ext4

option.name: -T
tip: Set the usage type so mke2fs can choose optimal parameters.
Usage types are defined in /etc/mke2fs.conf.

option.name: -U
tip: Set the file system UUID.
Possible values: clear, random, time
Any explicit UUID is also accepted.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose execution.

option.name: -V
tip: Print the version number and exit.

option.name: -z
tip: Write the old contents of each block to an undo file.
